Phase-1 baseline (CPU-only, no DB), 10 MiB fixtures, median of n=3, established
BEFORE any per-format optimization in this pass. Captured after fixing two
real regressions found during inspection:
  1. evidence_store.py: mixed string/datetime timestamp bug re-introduced by
     commit 2e8d325 ("replace timestamp re-parse with direct filter") - fixed
     by restoring parse_timestamp(event.timestamp).
  2. diagnostic_adapters.py _is_json_lines(): large compact single-document
     JSON/HAR (no newlines, first forced-split chunk >= MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_RECORD_BYTES
     and unparseable on its own) was incorrectly guessed as JSON-lines,
     silently shredding it into ~10 garbage text records instead of the real
     47,662 HAR entries. Fixed by falling through to document mode instead of
     guessing JSON-lines from size alone.

Confirms the task's core observation: GENERIC (tokenizer + retention gate)
is 2.5-5x faster than every other text format at equivalent size, because
every other format's normalizer still runs the full _classify_text() +
_extract_diagnostic_fields() machinery unconditionally per record, with no
early retention gate.

    JSON-document/BROWSER (median of n=3) ===

Verified via scripts/verify_structured_gate.py: 0 content mismatches, 0
evidence-loss risk across both fixtures' full record sets, 0 violations
across 21 adversarial payload shapes including the specific risk case this
gate's design accounts for (status resolves to INFO, but message text
carries its own competing level word - normalize_text_event's message-text
search always wins over a status-derived level, so the gate double-checks
the message for a level marker before ever skipping on status alone).

=== Source ZIP prep / build_index / correlate_event ===
Synthetic repo (scripts/bench_source.py): 2002 files, 13,902,668 bytes,
2,070,216-byte zip. All numbers median of n=5 (build_index/validate/extract)
or n=6 interleaved A/B trials (build_index, correlate_event) via
scripts/ab_build_index.py and scripts/ab_correlate.py.

validate_source_zip: 0.0053s (unchanged, not touched - already single
  linear infolist() scan with early size/count bounds)

extract_zip: 0.2314s (unchanged - see REVERTED EXPERIMENT below)

build_index:
  old (per-file Path.relative_to()):         median 0.1116s
  new (per-directory hoisted os.path.relpath): median 0.0328s
  delta: -70.6% (consistent across all 8 interleaved trials, zero overlap:
  old min 0.1056s > new max 0.0569s)
  Change: hoist the relative-directory computation to once per os.walk()
  directory instead of recomputing full_path.relative_to(root) per file.
  Path(filename).suffix/.stem deliberately left untouched (verified they
  diverge from os.path.splitext() on trailing-dot filenames - not worth the
  risk for a smaller win).
  Verified byte-identical by_path/by_suffix/by_stem across all 2002 files
  (scripts/ verified inline, see session notes).

correlate_event (20,000 events each, context-cache key Path -> str):
  unique-files scenario: old median 0.2346-0.2683s -> new median 0.0878-
    0.1053s (-60.8% to -62.6% across two runs)
  repeated-hot-file scenario: old median 0.2179-0.2324s -> new median
    0.0717-0.0722s (-66.9% to -69.2% across two runs)
  Change: SourceIndex._context_cache is now keyed by relative_path (str)
  instead of an absolute Path object. Path.__hash__ re-parses and
  re-normcases the whole string on every call and a fresh Path was being
  constructed (index.root / relative_path) for every single correlate call
  even on a cache hit; string keys make cache hits skip Path construction
  entirely. The absolute Path is now only built on a cache miss (real stat +
  read).
  Verified 0 mismatches in returned match dicts (snippet/context_start/
  context_end/etc) across all 40,000 events (unique + hot), old vs new,
  same synthetic index.

=== Resume correctness fix: idempotent prepare_source ===
process_analysis can legitimately be re-invoked for an analysis still in
"processing" status (Celery retry after worker crash/redelivery; artifacts
already resume correctly via processed_bytes/last_processed_line). But
_prepare_source_index called prepare_source() unconditionally on every
invocation, which was actually broken on resume, not just slow:
  - GitHub: git clone refuses a non-empty destination directory, so a
    resumed run for a GitHub-sourced analysis would always crash with
    SourceInputError instead of continuing.
  - ZIP: the staged upload is deleted after prepare_source's first success
    (_remove_staged_source_archive), so a resumed run would crash trying to
    reopen a file that no longer exists.
Fixed in source_archive.prepare_source(): a ready marker written beside
(not inside) the analysis-scoped dest dir after a full successful
clone/extract. On a later call, if the marker exists, skip straight to
build_index(dest) - no re-clone, no re-extract, no network call, just the
already-optimized local indexing step. If dest exists but the marker
doesn't (crashed/partial prior attempt), dest is discarded and redone from
scratch rather than silently reused. Covered by three new tests in
test_source_correlation.py: skip-reclone-on-resume (github), skip-
reextract-after-upload-deleted (zip), and discard-partial-dest-from-a-
crashed-prior-attempt (proves the fix doesn't paper over a truly incomplete
prior attempt). All 107 tests pass (104 baseline + 3 new).

=== GitHub source: network vs local CPU time (scripts/bench_github_source.py) ===
_clone_github() is a single `git clone --depth 1 --single-branch --no-tags`
subprocess call - already shallow, no other application CPU work in the
clone step itself. Real network clones against public GitHub repos (this
sandbox has outbound network access):

repo                  files   bytes        clone(net+git)   build_index(local)   local_share
pallets/flask (git)   230     2,744,272    2.854s           0.0050s              0.17%
django/django (git)   7,007   60,568,022   9.980s            0.2291s              2.24%

Network clone time is not application CPU time and is not something this
pass optimizes (per the task's explicit instruction) - it is bounded only
by the already-in-place --depth 1 shallow clone, GitHub's own transfer
speed, and GITHUB_CLONE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. The only local-CPU-bound step is
build_index(dest), which is the exact same function (and the exact same
70.6%-faster implementation) used for ZIP-sourced analyses. GitHub source
prep is therefore already using the optimized path with no separate work
needed, and local CPU is a negligible fraction (<2.5% here) of total
GitHub source prep time even before counting diagnostic ingestion.

=== Per-format batching benchmark (scripts/bench_batching.py) ===
Real MySQL, real process_analysis() end-to-end, only create_batches()'s
max_batch_bytes/max_batch_items varied. Median of n=3 wall-clock seconds per
10 MiB fixture:

format     small (1MiB/2000)   current (10MiB/20000)   large (50MiB/100000)
generic    6.642s              6.076s (-8.5%)          6.004s (-1.2% more)
database   3.974s              3.456s (-13.0%)         3.294s (-4.7% more)
ci_cd      3.359s              2.426s (-27.8%)         2.301s (-5.2% more)

Conclusion: KEPT the current defaults (INGESTION_RAW_BATCH_BYTES=10MiB,
INGESTION_RAW_BATCH_ITEMS=20000) unchanged - no code change made. Small
batches are a clear, material regression (8.5%-27.8% slower) from excess
commit/round-trip overhead, so the existing default is doing real work, not
guesswork. Going larger than current buys only 1.2%-5.2% more, which is
noise-adjacent for a real-DB benchmark and not "material" per the task's own
bar - and it comes at a real cost the task explicitly warned against:
courser checkpoint granularity (more re-work lost per crash) and, for the
~1 GiB uploads this deployment must support, holding a much larger
in-flight batch of ParsedEvent/Evidence-row objects in memory at once on an
~8 GiB shared box. Not worth it for a low single-digit-percent gain.

=== DB execution: N+1 / commit cost verification (task 17) ===
Read every function in the persistence hot path (evidence_store.py,
identity_persister.py, app/tasks/analysis.py's batch/artifact loops):
  - persist_evidence_batch(): ONE bulk `INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`
    executed via db.execute(statement, rows) with all of a batch's grouped
    rows passed together (SQLAlchemy executemany) - not a per-row loop.
  - persist_resolved_identities(): ONE set-based `UPDATE ... WHERE
    resolved_identity IS NULL` - not a per-row loop, no ORM object
    loading/refresh.
  - _assign_batch_fingerprints(): pure in-memory Python with a per-batch
    cache keyed on (exception_type, exception_message) or (level,
    raw_line) - zero DB calls.
  - Artifact loop: artifacts loaded with ONE `db.query(...).all()` up
    front, no per-artifact query inside the loop.
  - No `.refresh()` calls anywhere in the ingestion hot path.
  - Commits: exactly one db.commit() per batch (bundles the Evidence bulk
    upsert AND the artifact/analysis checkpoint-offset update into the same
    transaction, not two separate round trips), plus one at format-detect
    time and one at artifact-completion time per artifact. This is
    intentional checkpoint durability, already covered by the batching
    benchmark above - not N+1.
Verdict: no N+1 pattern anywhere in the write path. Confirmed by direct code
reading, not just benchmark inference.

=== Identity resolution: explaining the ~0.00s (task 18) ===
scripts/bench_pipeline.py full --iterations 3 against real MySQL, 10 MiB
GENERIC fixture, 13,233 evidence rows: identity stage median = 0.005s.
This is real, not a disabled/bypassed feature: persist_evidence_batch()
already resolves resolved_identity/identity_match_type/identity_strength
at INSERT time for every row where trace_id or request_id is known (same
precedence identity_persister.py applies), because that data is already in
hand before the row exists. persist_resolved_identities() only has to
catch the remainder: rows where NEITHER trace_id nor request_id was
present, whose "unresolved:<id>" identity string needs the DB-assigned row
id and so genuinely cannot be computed before the insert. For this
fixture, of 13,233 rows, only 2 were "unresolved" (9,924 trace_id + 3,307
request_id already resolved at insert). The identity pass's bulk UPDATE
WHERE resolved_identity IS NULL naturally does ~nothing when almost
nothing is unresolved - that's correct behavior, not a broken/no-op stage.
(Aside: this also explains why scripts/bench_pipeline.py's evidence_hash
check reports "not consistent" across repeated runs of the SAME fixture -
those 2 unresolved rows' identity strings embed Evidence.id, a fresh
DB-assigned auto-increment value each run, so their string content
legitimately differs run to run even though row count, and every other
row's content, is 100% consistent. Not a Devflo bug - a benchmark-hash
methodology quirk worth noting so it isn't mistaken for one.)

=== Timeline processing: confirmed no-op (task 19) ===
app/services/timeline_processor.py's process_persisted_timelines() is a
literal `return` with no body. Measured 0.000s, consistent with the code,
not "optimized to near-zero" - there was never any work here to optimize.
Left untouched per the task's explicit instruction not to restore/build out
timeline processing (out of scope) and not to misrepresent this as this
pass's work.

REVERTED EXPERIMENT: _extract_zip's Path.resolve() (37% of extraction time
per cProfile) was replaced with os.path.realpath() wrapped in Path(). This
produced byte-identical resolved paths (differential-tested) and passed all
tests + a new symlink-escape security test, but a rigorous interleaved A/B
benchmark (scripts/ab_extract_zip.py, 6 trials each) showed it was
CONSISTENTLY SLOWER (6/6 trials), median regression -6.9%. Reverted per the
absolute regression rule; only the new symlink-escape test
(test_extract_zip_rejects_escape_via_preexisting_symlink) was kept, since it
has independent security value. Re-profiling _extract_zip after the
build_index/correlate_event wins shows lstat()/mkdir()/open()/decompress/
write dominating - this is now genuinely I/O- and security-check-bound
(zip-slip containment requires real path resolution per file), not a
low-hanging algorithmic win, and is left untouched.
